intro.p1:
"Travel insurance is too expensive..."
"I just want coverage for minor sickness and accidents."
intro.p2:
Heading to Thailand soon? One item you simply cannot leave Japan without is the right **Credit Card**.
Did you know that you can get **90 days of overseas medical insurance** for free, just by using your card for airport transport?
intro.p3:
In this guide, we've hand-picked the **3 essential cards** that every Digital TOTONOI THAI should carry.
Having these cards alone can save you roughly **30,000 to 50,000 JPY ($200-$350)** in insurance premiums per trip.

insurance_system.title: Critical: "Automatic" vs. "Utilization" Coverage
insurance_system.desc: Not all card insurance is the same. Since late 2023, many cards have switched to "Utilization-based" coverage. Knowing the difference is crucial to ensure you are covered.

automatic.label: Automatic Coverage (e.g. Rakuten Premium)
automatic.desc: The insurance is active just by **holding** the card. No action needed. Most common in Gold/Platinum cards.

utilization.label: Utilization Coverage (e.g. Epos Card)
utilization.desc: The insurance activates ONLY if you **pay for travel transport** (like the train/bus to the airport) with the card. This is now the industry standard.

insurance_system.conclusion: Pro Tip: Use a "Utilization" card to pay for your train to Narita/Haneda to activate the insurance before you fly.

insurance_flow_detail.title: Beginner's Guide: How to Use Free Card Insurance
insurance_flow_detail.lead:
Worried strictly about the "Utilization" rule? Don't be.
It's as simple as buying a train ticket. Here is the 4-step process from departure to seeing a doctor.

step1.title: Step 1: Activate Before You Fly
step1.desc:
Pay for your **Airport Train (Skyliner, NEX)** or **Limousine Bus** with your card. Even a few hundred yen bus ticket counts.
*Tip: Buy at the ticket machine or counter directly. Suica top-ups often don't count.*
step1.pro_tip: 💡 For Epos Card, simply paying for the train to the airport activates your full insurance coverage!

step2.title: Step 2: If You Get Sick in Thailand
step2.desc:
Before going to a hospital, call the **24/7 Emergency Desk** (number on back of card).
Ask for a **"Cashless Treatment"** appointment. They will find a nearby hospital and handle the billing directly.
step2.note: ⚠️ Always call first! If you go directly, you might have to pay upfront and claim later.

step3.title: Step 3: At the Hospital
step3.desc:
Show your **Passport** and **Credit Card** (plus insurance certificate if you printed it) at reception.
Since billing is handled between the insurance and the hospital, you simply receive treatment and medicine for **Free**. Just sign the receipt.

step4.title: Step 4: After Returning Home
step4.desc:
If you used Cashless Treatment, there is usually no paperwork needed after you return.
*If you paid upfront, you will need to mail the receipts to claim your refund.*

insurance_flow_detail.cta_text: If you don't have a reliable card yet, the Epos Card is the safest bet for high coverage.

epos.name: Epos Card
points: Medical Limit: Max 2.7 Million JPY (Gold-tier level)
epos.desc: The single best free card for travel insurance. Although it requires "Utilization" (paying for transport), the **2.7 Million JPY** medical coverage is incredibly high for a free card. A must-have for every Expat.

rakuten.name: Rakuten Premium Card
rakuten.desc: The cheapest way to get a **Priority Pass** for airport lounge access. While visits are now limited to 5 times/year, the comfort of free food, drinks, and Wi-Fi in lounges makes it easily worth the 11,000 JPY fee for any regular traveler.

marriott.name: Marriott Bonvoy Amex
marriott.catch: [Luxury] Best for Miles & Free Hotel Stays
points: Benefit: Annual Free Night Award (Luxury Hotels)
Miles: High transfer rate to 40+ airlines (JAL/ANA/United)
marriott.desc: The ultimate card for travel hackers. The fee is high, but the **Free Night Award** and exceptional mile accumulation rate make it efficient for those who fly frequently or love staying at Ritz-Carlton/Marriott hotels.

cta.title: Start with the Epos Card
cta.desc:
Zero annual fee. Zero risk. High coverage.
It is the perfect "Guardian Charm" for your travels. Apply now and activate your insurance with your train ticket.

warning.title: Important: 90-Day Limit
warning.desc:
Credit card insurance typically covers you for **90 days** from departure.
If you plan to stay in Thailand longer than 3 months, you MUST switch to a Expat insurance like **SafetyWing**. Staying uninsured is a major financial risk.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Q. Is it hard to get approved?
faq.a1: A. Epos and Rakuten are known for being relatively foreigner and freelancer-friendly. However, it is always safest to apply while you still have employment status in Japan.
faq.q2: Q. Do I need an Insurance Certificate?
faq.a2: A. Yes. While the card itself is proof, downloading the **English Insurance Certificate (PDF)** from the card's website and printing it is highly recommended for smoother hospital acceptance.
faq.q3: Q. Should I avoid 'Revolving Payment' cards?
faq.a3: A. Yes. Some cards default to 'Revo' (Revolving) payments which incur high interest. Make sure to set your payment method to **"One-time payment" (Ikkatsu)** in the card settings.
